resources.string: Optional. Recognises on this device whether a video is practice, education, news, entertainment and so on. Nothing leaves the device. It only ever adds warnings or ordering and never decides on its own; without the model ZenPipe works exactly as before.
Not available on this device (needs Android 7 and a 64-bit processor).
Not installed. The model download is not published yet.
Download the content recognition model (about %1$d MB) from GitHub? This is the only connection the content recognition ever makes; nothing about you or your videos is sent. Wi-Fi recommended.
Delete the content recognition model? ZenPipe then works as without it; you can download it again at any time.
No video classified yet. New feed videos are classified in the background after a feed refresh; opened videos with their description.

Latest classifications (newest first): categories with confidence · tone · feed weight · input (T = title and channel only, D = with description). Second line: strongest topics and formats. The recognition is wrong for about one video in seven.
Content recognition: order the feed by content (news and entertainment further back)
Content recognition: limit distressing videos (at most 1 in 10, never two in a row, not at the top)
The two content switches are in the list above. Turning them off is a loosening (takes effect after 24 hours). Without a working model the feed is ordered exactly as before.
To delete the model, first turn off both content switches above (a loosening that takes effect after 24 hours).
Content recognition: loading the newest videos …

The content recognition sees only %1$d of %2$d newer videos of \"%3$s\" as practice (follow-along, breathing, meditation, falling asleep). %4$d look like entertainment or news, e.g. \"%5$s\".\n\nThe recognition is wrong for about every fourth video. Practice videos are exempt from the feed limits and the mandatory pause. Please only mark channels and playlists you really use for practising.
